- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days); add 1-2% buffer to forecast following such events.  
- Model overestimates in early horizon (first 5-7 days) after strong sentiment shifts; apply downward adjustment of 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days post-sentiment shift.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish then bearish” cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment weight to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply “sustained breakout” rule: add 0.5–1.0% to next forecast to capture momentum.
